chapter: Lucky Millinder and Duke Ellington's band, 1948-52
title: Waiting on unemployment and Duke's offer to replace Claude Jones
summary: After Ellington returned from Europe he offered Jackson Claude Jones's chair; Jones was unhappy being made to play valve trombone.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: So then I waited around New York and just waited around, and me and unemployment insurance made it.

And when Duke came back from Europe, I called him and asked him did he want me in the band. And then he told me yes, he said, 'You're going to take Claude Jones' place.' And I said, 'Oh, gee, I didn't want to do that,' you know, because, gee whiz, I mean Claude, you know --

Oh, God. Then I got to thinking and I said -- Well, I knew Claude wasn't getting along over there. I knew that too, you know. There was a little jealous thing going on in there, you know, between him and Lawrence, I found out later, because he didn't want to play a valve trombone and Duke wanted him to play valve trombone because Tizol played valve and that's what he wanted in that particular chair, you see. And so Claude didn't really get to play solos like he wanted to, you know.
And so I said, 'Well,' and I went to meet the band in
the Duke Ellington club in Washington and I took Claude's place in the band, and I was playing --
